subtasks.title: Investigate IsHumanGate dependencies and comment-status coupling
subtasks.description:
Before removing the status gate, investigate all code paths that depend on comments only existing on human-gate statuses. Search for:

1. All callers of IsHumanGate() — confirm only AddComment (task_api.go:18) and TUI handleAddComment (actions.go:221) enforce the restriction
2. Notification or webhook systems that filter comments by status
3. Audit trail or logging that assumes comments are gate-only
4. Permission checks or visibility rules that depend on comment-status coupling
5. Workflow engine code that reads comments and assumes gate context
6. Git history around the original gate implementation — was it a deliberate workflow requirement or implementation convenience?

Produce a brief impact report as a code comment at the top of the implementation PR or in the commit message. If any hidden dependencies are found, flag them before proceeding.

Acceptance: Documented evidence that no subsystem depends on comments being restricted to gate statuses, or a list of additional changes needed.

subtasks.title: Write tests for removing AddComment status gate and TUI gate
subtasks.description:
Update and extend tests to define expected behavior after removing the status gate from AddComment and the TUI handleAddComment.

Changes to existing tests:
1. Update TestAddComment_WrongStatus (lifecycle_test.go:1130-1140) — this test currently asserts that AddComment fails on StatusInProgress. After the gate removal, it should assert SUCCESS. Rename to TestAddComment_AnyStatus or similar and verify the comment is persisted.

New TUI tests:
2. Add TestModelWiring_HandleAddComment_NonGateStatus in model_wiring_test.go — verify that handleAddComment opens the feedback dialog for a task in StatusInProgress (non-gate status). Currently the TUI silently returns nil for non-gate statuses.
3. Add TestModelWiring_HandleAddComment_NeedsClarification — verify the clarification UX path is still preserved (StatusNeedsClarification should open with the clarification title).

The existing 508a2c0 tests (TestAddComment_BacklogStatus through TestAddComment_RejectedStatus in lifecycle_test.go:1509-1863) already cover all 14 statuses and edge cases. They currently fail because the gate is still in place — they will pass after implementation.

All tests should use testutil infrastructure (NewTestDB, etc.) per architecture constitution.

subtasks.title: Remove status gate from AddComment and TUI handleAddComment
subtasks.description:
Remove the IsHumanGate() status restriction from two locations, allowing comments on tasks in any status.

1. internal/orchestrator/task_api.go (lines 18-20): Remove the 3-line block:
   ```
   if !task.Status.IsHumanGate() {
       return fmt.Errorf("add comment: task %s is in %s, comments only allowed in human-gate statuses", taskID, task.Status)
   }
   ```
   Update the function's doc comment to remove 'Only allowed for human-gate statuses.'

2. internal/tui/actions.go (line 221): Remove the IsHumanGate() check from handleAddComment. The function currently returns early with `return m, nil` for non-gate statuses. After removal, all statuses should proceed to the feedback dialog. Preserve the StatusNeedsClarification special-case UX (lines 225-237) — it opens a clarification answer dialog instead of a generic comment dialog.

   The revised logic should be:
   - If selected is nil, return early
   - If StatusNeedsClarification, open clarification answer dialog (existing behavior)
   - Otherwise, open generic 'Add Comment' dialog (now works for ALL statuses)

Do NOT modify or remove IsHumanGate() itself — it has other callers.
Do NOT modify the pre-written tests — fix implementation to match tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Comments can be added to tasks in any status
- No regression in existing comment functionality
- Clarification UX preserved for StatusNeedsClarification

subtasks.title: Integration: end-to-end verification and documentation
subtasks.description:
Final integration subtask that wires together the changes and documents the behavior change.

1. Run the full test suite to verify:
   - All 508a2c0 tests pass (TestAddComment_BacklogStatus through TestAddComment_MultipleCommentsOnTask)
   - Updated TestAddComment_WrongStatus (now expects success) passes
   - New TUI wiring tests pass
   - Existing gate-status tests still pass (TestAddComment_GateStatus_*)
   - No regressions in lifecycle_test.go or model_wiring_test.go

2. Documentation: Update docs/README.md or the relevant API documentation section to note:
   - AddComment now accepts comments on tasks in ANY status (not just human-gate statuses)
   - The StatusNeedsClarification UX flow is preserved in the TUI
   - This change enables programmatic agent use (C-Suite agents, temp workers) to annotate tasks during any lifecycle phase

3. Verify the clarification UX flow end-to-end: a task in StatusNeedsClarification should still open the clarification answer dialog in the TUI.

This subtask is simple integration wiring — the feature is a constraint removal, not new module creation. No new subsystem connections are needed; the integration verifies the removed constraint doesn't break existing flows.

assumptions.decision: Update TestAddComment_WrongStatus to expect success rather than deleting it
alternatives: Delete the test entirely since the gate no longer exists
Keep the test as-is and add a skip annotation
assumptions.why_chosen: Renaming and updating the test to assert success on non-gate statuses provides positive coverage and documents the new behavior. Deleting would reduce coverage.

assumptions.decision: Add TUI wiring tests for non-gate status comment flow
alternatives: Only test the orchestrator layer, trust TUI follows
Add full Bubble Tea integration tests with tea.Program
assumptions.why_chosen: The TUI has its own gate check independent of the orchestrator. A wiring test verifies the dialog opens for non-gate statuses without the overhead of full TUI integration testing. Matches existing test patterns in model_wiring_test.go.

docs/README.md is the user-facing documentation. The change affects API behavior (AddComment no longer rejects non-gate statuses) which users and agents need to know about. ARCHITECTURE.md describes structural rules, not API behavior.

assumptions.decision: Research subtask runs first to validate removal is safe before writing tests or code
alternatives: Skip research and proceed directly to implementation
Combine research into the implementation subtask

A dedicated research subtask ensures hidden dependencies are found before code changes, preventing rework. Separating it allows the researcher agent to focus on investigation without implementation concerns.
